title: Add NVTX ranges and microbench harness for runtime profiling and KV-cache metrics
author: Sofia Patel
description:
Motivation: We need finer-grained, low-overhead profiling in the serving runtime to identify per-kernel hotspots and validate scheduling/batching heuristics on real workloads. This PR adds NVTX ranges around hot paths (kernels, continuous batching loop, scheduler enqueue/dequeue, KV cache lookup/insert) and a small microbenchmark harness for deterministic per-kernel timing and KV-cache throughput measurements. It also adds counters exported to our perf job so we can track KV cache hit rates and batching efficiency over time. The description below covers the implementation, usage, and early results.

Implementation summary:
- NVTX: lightweight NVTX ranges inserted into runtime/src/serving/runtime_profiler.{cc,h} around: attention kernel launch, quantized kernel launch, KV cache lookup/insert, batching loop boundaries, scheduler wake/enqueue, and GPU memcpy regions. Ranges are no-op when NVTX is disabled at build/runtime.
- Counters: a small set of atomic counters (KV_CACHE_HITS, KV_CACHE_LOOKUPS, BATCHED_REQUESTS, CONT_BATCH_CYCLES) exposed via the existing runtime metrics exporter. Counters are incremented in hot paths with minimal overhead and aggregated per-worker.
- Microbench harness: tools/microbench/kv_cache_bench.cc and tools/microbench/kernel_timer.cc which run short deterministic workloads (synthetic KV access patterns, single-token generation loops, and small to medium batch generation) and emit CSV timing and NVTX-marked traces. The harness can run locally or in CI using the perf job container.
- Perf CI integration: infra/ci/perf-job.yaml adds a nightly perf job that runs the microbench on a dedicated perf-GPU node, collects CSV/trace artifacts, and uploads them to our internal perf-dashboard ingestion pipeline.
- Dashboards and docs: docs/perf/profiling.md documents how to interpret NVTX traces and counters. Grafana dashboard (internal link) added to visualize KV cache hit rate, batching efficiency, and p95/p99 kernel latencies.

Example usage: ./bazel run //tools/microbench:kv_cache_bench -- --model=resnet-like --workload=short --iterations=500

Artifacts: The perf job uploads CSVs and .nvtx traces that we view in Nsight Systems and our Grafana perf dashboard.

Key implementation notes:
- NVTX scopes are guarded and compiled out if NVTX is not available to keep builds portable.
- We intentionally keep per-invocation NVTX insertion minimal to keep overhead <1% on microbench.

Microbench results (sample):
- Small-batch (batch=1..4) synthetic GPT-like workload: p95 latency reduced 8-12% after small scheduler micro-optimizations identified using traces (reduced lock contention and fewer context switches).
- KV-cache instrumentation showed a 22% hit-rate on a sampled prompt set; enabling prefix caching on the workload reduced token compute by ~10% on average.
- Continuous batching counters helped identify a pathological workload with many short-lived requests; after tuning the batch flush threshold we improved throughput by ~6% and lowered p99 tail latency by ~15%.

Commits and summary of changes:
- Add runtime_profiler.{cc,h} NVTX range helpers and atomic counters
- Thread-safe counter exports and metrics integration
- Microbench tools for KV-cache and kernel timings
- Perf CI job and artifact upload step
- Documentation and dashboard

JSON Example small snippet added to runtime_profiler.cc: "// NVTX scoped range for attention kernel\nNVTX_RANGE(\"attention_kernel\");\nlaunch_attention_kernel(...);"

Backwards compatibility: NVTX instrumentation is optional and guarded; counters use existing metrics plumbing. No API changes to customers.

Review and discussion highlights:
- Liam: asked for validation that NVTX overhead is negligible; I ran microbench with/without NVTX and added results to the perf artifacts showing <0.8% overhead on avg.
- Marisol: requested per-worker aggregation so the dashboard shows pooled worker metrics; added aggregation and clarified in docs.
- Ethan: asked to ensure counters are zero-cost when metrics exporter is disabled; added conditional increments and compile guards.

CI:
- Unit tests: pass
- Integration tests: pass (small runtime smoke tests)
- Lint/format: pass

Merge: Squash merge into main (see merge_commit)

release_notes:
- Adds NVTX ranges to key runtime hot paths for GPU tracing.
- Adds microbenchmark harness for KV cache and kernel timing.
- Exposes KV cache hit counters and batching efficiency metrics.
- Adds nightly perf CI job and uploads artifacts to the perf dashboard.
notes: This PR is part of the runtime perf initiative (ENG-1245). The microbench and NVTX traces were instrumental in identifying locking contention in the scheduler and in validating small scheduler micro-optimizations that yielded measurable p95 improvements on tail-heavy workloads. Next steps: add sample-based collection for long-running production traces, expand microbench workloads to multi-GPU scenarios, and add alerting on KV cache regression thresholds.
